subject: Re: Nexa RFP - Dedicated capacity questionnaire and sizing questions
messages:
From: Sanjay Ramaswamy <sanjay.r@nexa.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexa Procurement <procurement@nexa.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - high level workload and targets

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is our questionnaire (Nexa_RFP_Dedicated_Questions.pdf). A few high-level bullets up front to help you prioritize answers inside the pack:

- Workload: customer-facing assistant + summarization. Mostly text generation and reranking across English.
- Expected steady-state: ~250 requests per second (qps) to the generate endpoint, average request ~200 tokens output.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms (preferred), p99 <= 250ms.
- Burst behavior: occasional spikes up to ~1,000 qps for 5-20 minute windows (market open/closing traffic).
- Desired commitment: reserved/dedicated pool with burst credits. 12- to 24-month term negotiable.
- Data residency: US-East (need VPC option).

Can you provide: GPU family recommendations (A100/H100/L4 etc) and a mapping of expected steady-state throughput per GPU, recommended pool size for steady-state + burst plan, guidance on quantization and expected quality delta, and an estimate of committed vs burst pricing (ballpark is fine). Also include any operational runbooks for failover and canary rollouts.

Please send the completed questionnaire and any supporting sizing workbook. Procurement needs the numbers to evaluate cost and commitment options.

Thanks,
Sanjay R.
VP, Platform Engineering
Nexa Financial Systems

Attachment: Nexa_RFP_Dedicated_Questions.pdf (PDF, 480KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - initial sizing proposal

Team — forwarding Nexa's top-line ask. I drafted an initial approach below. Please review and flag any improvements; I want to send a consolidated answer back to Sanjay by EOD Friday.

Quoted message:
> On Tue, 30 Mar 2027 at 15:02, Sanjay Ramaswamy <sanjay.r@nexa.com> wrote:
> > (see attached)

My proposed mapping (first-pass, conservative):
- Workload assumptions: 250 steady qps, 200 tokens per request average, mix of short chat and longer summarization (20% long-form).
- Kernel assumptions: our runtime (OPT-kernel + KV prefix caching) yields ~20-30% token-level savings for repeat conversational prefixes; estimateKV cache reduces token compute by ~25% on this mix.

GPU sizing options (steady-state effective QPS after caching):
- H100 (80GB, fp16/nf4): assume 1 H100 -> ~45 effective qps at 200 tokens (optimistic, low-batch latency-tuned).
- A100 (80GB, fp16/int8): assume 1 A100 -> ~32 effective qps at 200 tokens (slower kernels for some model variants).
- Cost-optimal blend: 6 x H100 + 4 x A100 for steady-state of ~6*45 + 4*32 = ~410 qps capacity (after KV savings). This gives ~1.6x headroom over the 250 baseline for growth and maintenance windows.

Burst strategy:
- Reserved pool: size for steady-state + modest headroom (we recommend sizing to ~1.25x steady = ~313 qps).
- Burst credit lane (on-demand or burst VMs): allow autoscale to add up to additional 700 qps (equivalent to ~12 extra H100-equivalents) for short windows. Use a 2-stage routing policy: (1) route to reserved pool until saturation threshold, (2) burst into on-demand dedicated fleet.

Quantization / quality guidance:
- Recommend nf4 / int8 options for lower-cost inference for non-critical summarization flows. Expect a mean metric delta of 1-3% on Rouge/BLEU-type metrics and subjective quality drop of 2-5% for complex context-sensitive completions.

Operational notes:
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with rollback hooks and prompt-set based quality checks.
- Tail-latency controls: small-batch fast-paths with soft-priority preemption for low-latency calls.

Attachments: I attached a working sizing workbook (nexa-sizing-workbook.xlsx) with throughput tables and cost model estimates. Please review the per-GPU throughput numbers and comment.

Key questions for Priyom / Grace / Aisha:
- Priyom: do you agree with the per-GPU qps numbers for our 200-token model? Any kernel tuning we should call out?
- Grace: can you validate the burst lane sizing and suggested autoscale guardrails?
- Aisha: procurement/term recommendations and pricing cadence (committed vs burst).

Thanks — Logan

Attachment: nexa-sizing-workbook.xlsx (Excel, 320KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - initial sizing proposal

Logan — quick notes after running the workbook through our perf models:

- Per-GPU throughput: H100 @ 80GB with our perf kernel and nf4 quantization (where acceptable) is about 48 qps (200-token / latency-optimized path) if we allow batching up to 8 tokens average micro-batch. If client insists on strict p99 < 250ms without batching, drop to 36 qps per H100.
- A100 numbers are roughly 28-34 qps depending on kernel and whether we use int8.
- Recommendation: offer two SKUs:
  1) Performance SKU: all-H100 (8–10 units) targeted for strict latency/p99 use cases.
  2) Value SKU: H100 + A100 blend (e.g., 6 H100 + 6 A100) with autoscale burst to on-demand for extended spikes.

- On quantization: nf4 is our preferred default for most flows; call out model validation step for customer to approve quality. We'll include a prompt-set regression test as part of the QPS acceptance criteria.

- Commitment terms: 12-month reservation with a 20% discount to on-demand and a burst allowance (hours-per-month) is the typical structure. If Nexa wants 24-month we can move to 30% discount.

I'll add these tightened numbers into the workbook and include a small appendix about kernel tuning knobs.

— Priyom

Subject: Re: Nexa RFP - Dedicated capacity questionnaire and sizing questions

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the questionnaire. Attached are our completed responses and a recommended sizing workbook. Key highlights below:

1) Recommended configurations (final):
- Performance SKU (latency-critical): 10 x H100 (80GB, nf4) reserved pool. Estimated steady-state capacity: ~360 qps (no batching), headroom for short peaks. p95/p99 meet Nexa's SLOs on our latency-optimized kernel.
- Value SKU (cost-aware): 6 x H100 + 6 x A100 reserved. Estimated steady-state capacity: ~360–400 qps after KV caching benefits (effective). Lower unit cost but slightly larger p99 tail under identical traffic patterns.

2) Burst plan and autoscale:
- We size the reserved commitment to cover steady-state + 25% buffer. For short bursts up to ~1,000 qps we recommend an on-demand burst pool that can be called via policy. Typical burst lane equals roughly 12 H100-equivalents for 15–30 minute windows.

3) Quantization & quality:
- Default recommendation: nf4 for inference; int8 for cheaper, non-critical summarization flows. Expect subjective quality delta of 2–5% for high-complexity completions when moving from fp16 to nf4/int8. We will run Nexa's provided prompt set and report regression numbers as part of acceptance testing.

4) Ops and runbook:
- Included: canary rollout recipe (5/25/100%), prompt-based regression checks, automatic fallback to smaller model variants with explicit quality warnings, and a PG-run playbook for failover to another region. See attached redwood-dedicated-runbook.pdf.

5) Commercials (ballpark):
- 12-month reserved (Performance SKU): estimated $XX,XXX/month (detailed breakdown in workbook).
- Burst credits/on-demand: metered at on-demand rates; we provide an hours-per-month burst allowance in the contract. Exact pricing to be defined with procurement.

Attachments: completed questionnaire (Nexa_RFP_Dedicated_Questions.pdf), sizing workbook (nexa-sizing-workbook.xlsx), runbook (redwood-dedicated-runbook.pdf), draft commitment term sheet (nexa-commitment-term-sheet.docx).

Next steps:
- If acceptable, procurement can request a formal quote and term sheet — I'll loop Legal for the purchase order and DocuSign.
- We will schedule a technical validation session (3rd week of April) to run Nexa's prompt set and the acceptance benchmark.

Thanks — looking forward to feedback.

Best,
Logan Wright

Redwood Inference
